status_why: No statewide count on the night: each of the 21 county clerks posts its own; the Division posts official results after certification.

races_in_feed: the state publishes Congress and Senate only (no state legislature or governor on the 2026 ballot; odd-year offices). County sites carry county commissioners, clerks, sheriffs, surrogates, municipal councils, school boards and questions
local: yes, all 21: Bergen County Clerk (bergencountyclerk.org), Middlesex, Essex, Monmouth, Hudson, Ocean (addresses not yet confirmed)
how_counted: Each county clerk posts unofficial results as municipalities report; the state posts official results after certification.
vote_types: not on any state feed; some county sites split vote-by-mail, election day and provisional (unverified)

certify.body: the New Jersey State Board of Canvassers
certify.rule: Meets no later than 30 days after the election (N.J. Rev. Stat. 19:21-1).
certify.source: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself

scout_blocked: nj.gov answered scripts (200). elec.nj.gov (campaign finance) is behind Incapsula (CLAUDE.md), not the results.
scout_plan: Readable with care, county by county. New Jersey has no statewide election-night feed, so the U.S. Senate and twelve House races must be summed from the 21 county clerks' unofficial pages; a scout pass in October should find each county's results address and vendor (some are likely Clarity, which has a JSON feed) and write one small reader per layout, largest counties first. Where a county cannot be read, the page shows that county as 'not reporting here' rather than a partial sum. Official totals come from the Division's PDFs after certification. Local races ride on the same county pages.
